answer: Price influence quadratically: an agent's first unit of work weight costs one credit, the second costs four, the tenth costs a hundred, so splitting effort across a thousand clones buys less total influence than one honest identity spending the same budget. Each identity must also keep an onyx-hard audit trail, every completed job signed and publicly checkable, so clones hiding in a shared lagoon of fake activity are easy to spot: identical outputs and timing betray the shared operator, and a plume of evidence from independent auditors triggers slashing of the whole cluster at once.
